title: Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility — Non-Covered Notices, Filing Limits and Appeal Periods
content:
For each payer class of **Insurance Coverage & Patient Responsibility**, this table gives the instrument a patient must sign before an expected non-covered or upgraded item can be billed to the patient, whether upgrades may be billed at all, who absorbs the amount when the notice was missed, and the filing and appeal periods of the class.

## Notices and upgrades

| Payer class | Non-covered notice instrument | Upgrade billing permitted | Supplier absorbs the amount when the required notice was not signed before delivery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | ABN form | yes | yes |
| Medicare Advantage HMO | plan organization determination | yes | yes |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | plan organization determination | yes | yes |
| Medicaid Fee-for-Service | not permitted | no | yes |
| Commercial HMO | financial waiver | yes | yes |
| Commercial PPO | financial waiver | yes | yes |
| Medicare Supplement Plan G | follows the primary | yes | yes |

- **Non-covered notice instrument**: the instrument that must be signed before an expected non-covered or upgraded item can be billed to the patient. "Not permitted" and "follows the primary" are instrument values in their own right.
- **Upgrade billing permitted**: whether the patient may elect an upgraded item and pay the difference over the allowed amount of the covered item.
- **Supplier absorbs**: whether, when the required non-covered notice was not signed before delivery, the supplier absorbs the non-covered amount instead of the patient.

## Filing and appeal periods (calendar days unless stated)

| Payer class | Claim must reach the payer within (days after date of service) | First-level appeal may be filed within (days after initial denial) | Payer decides a first-level appeal within (days) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Original Medicare Part B | 365 | 120 | 60 |
| Medicare Advantage HMO | 180 | 65 | 30 |
| Medicare Advantage PPO | 180 | 65 | 30 |
| Medicaid Fee-for-Service | 180 | 60 | 45 |
| Commercial HMO | 90 | 180 | 30 |
| Commercial PPO | 180 | 180 | 30 |
| Medicare Supplement Plan G | 365 | 120 | 60 |

A first-level appeal is a redetermination or reconsideration. The filing period counts calendar days after the date of service within which the claim must reach the payer; the appeal window counts calendar days after the initial denial date.

## Example (hypothetical)

A Commercial HMO line with a date of service on the first day of a month must reach the payer within 90 calendar days after that date; had the line been billed to Original Medicare Part B, the period would be 365 days.
